chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī Ṣāliḥ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A group from Banī Ḍabbah came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله sick. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to them: “Stay with me, and when you recover, I will send you in a detachment.” They said: “Send us out from al-Madīnah.”

So he sent them to the camels of the sadaqah, so that they might drink from their urine and eat from their milk. Then when they recovered and became strong, they killed three of those who were with the camels. News reached the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, so he sent ʿAlī عليه السلام to them while they were in a valley, having become bewildered and unable to get out of it, near the land of Yemen. He captured them and brought them to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.

Then this verse was sent down upon him: “The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive in the earth spreading corruption is only that they be killed, or crucified, or that their hands and their feet be cut off on opposite sides.”

key_terms.أَبْوَالِهَا: their urine, used here as a treatment
key_terms.إِبِلِ الصَّدَقَةِ: the camels designated for sadaqah holdings
key_terms.سَرِيَّةٍ: a military detachment or expeditionary unit
key_terms.فَسَاداً: corruption and violent disorder in the land
key_terms.مِنْ خِلَافٍ: on opposite sides, meaning cross-limb punishment
key_terms.يُحَارِبُونَ: they wage war against or violently oppose

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning and context of the verse about those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and spread corruption in the land?
ai.summary: This narration presents an occasion connected to the revelation of the verse about those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and spread corruption in the land. It describes a group who were treated mercifully, then committed murder and banditry, after which the verse established the gravity and punishment of such public corruption.
